We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps correspond to forward reactions: 1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthesis: break amide bond to give acid and aniline (or amine). Then break the α,β-unsaturated acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the new alkene). So retrosynthetic step: cut the C=C double bond and the carboxylic acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid. Then sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride + aniline -> sulfonamide. So we need to identify fragments.

Target: aromatic ring A (p-tolyl) with sulfonamide linking to aromatic ring B (phenyl) bearing α,β-unsaturated amide side chain (C= C - C(=O)N-Ph-NH2?). Actually structure: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: p-tolyl (CH3 on phenyl) attached to N-sulfonyl group: NS(=O)(=O) attached to second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2). That second phenyl has a para substituent: /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N (i.e., trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide) with an NH2 ortho? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an extra NH2 at para? Wait: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with two amino groups? Actually c3ccccc3 is phenyl; N attached to phenyl at position 1, and there is another N attached to phenyl at position? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline where the phenyl has an NH attached at position 1 (the N before c3) and also an NH attached at position 6? Actually the SMILES: N c3 c c c c c3 N. So there are two amino groups on the phenyl (para? maybe 1,4). So the amide attaches to an aniline (anilide) which also has an NH2 para.

Thus retrosynthesis: Step 1 (forward amide formation): The α,β-unsaturated acid (C=C-COOH) reacts with aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) to give the amide. So retrosynthetic cleavage: break amide to give α,β-unsaturated acid (C=C-COOH) and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). The α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl B via the double bond: /C=C/ attached to phenyl B at the β carbon (i.e., phenyl B-CH=CH-COOH). So the fragment is phenyl B-CH=CH-COOH (trans). So step 1 yields two fragments: phenyl B-CH=CH-COOH (call fragment A) and aniline (para-diaminobenzene). Good.

Step 2 (Doebner modification): The α,β-unsaturated acid (phenyl-CH=CH-COOH) is formed from aromatic aldehyde (phenyl-CHO) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So retrosynthetic cleavage: break the C=C and the carboxyl to give phenyl-CHO and malonic acid. So fragment: phenyl-CHO (benzaldehyde) and malonic acid.

Step 3 (sulfonamide formation): The sulfonamide linking p-tolyl amine to phenyl B sulfonyl chloride. In forward, aniline (p-toluidine) reacts with sulfonyl chloride (ArSO2Cl) to give sulfonamide. So retrosynthetic cleavage: break N-S bond to give p-toluidine (CH3-Ph-NH2) and sulfonyl chloride (ArSO2Cl) where Ar is phenyl B (c2ccc(... )cc2). So fragment: phenyl B sulfonyl chloride (ArSO2Cl) and p-toluidine.

Thus overall route: Starting materials: p-toluidine, phenyl B sulfonyl chloride (which itself can be derived from phenyl B (the same phenyl that later gets the α,β-unsaturated acid). But we need 3 reactions total, so we must have sulfonyl chloride already available (maybe from phenyl B with SO2Cl). However we can consider that phenyl B sulfonyl chloride is derived from phenyl B (the same phenyl that will later be functionalized). But we have only 3 steps, so we need to produce phenyl B sulfonyl chloride from phenyl B (maybe via chlorosulfonation). But that would be a fourth step. However the guidance says three reactions: 1) amide formation, 2) Doebner modification, 3) sulfonamide formation. So they assume sulfonyl chloride is available as reagent (commercial). So we can propose route using commercially available sulfonyl chloride (e.g., 4-(2-carboxyvinyl)phenylsulfonyl chloride). But that sulfonyl chloride already contains the unsaturated acid? Actually we need sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl B which later will be functionalized via Doebner and amide. The sulfonyl chloride could be 4-(2-carboxyvinyl)phenylsulfonyl chloride? That would already have the unsaturated acid, but then amide formation would be after sulfonamide formation? The order in forward: first sulfonamide formation (makes sulfonamide linking p-tolyl to phenyl B). Then Doebner modification on phenyl B aldehyde? Wait the phenyl B after sulfonamide still has a substituent (the unsaturated acid) attached to the ring. The Doebner modification uses an aldehyde on that ring; but after sulfonamide formation, the ring still has an aldehyde? Actually the target has the unsaturated acid attached to phenyl B via double bond; that unsaturated acid is formed from aldehyde. So the aldehyde must be present before Doebner. So the sequence forward could be: start with phenyl B bearing aldehyde (4-formyl phenyl). Perform Doebner to get unsaturated acid attached. Then amide formation with aniline to give amide. Then sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride derived from phenyl B? Wait sulfonyl chloride must be attached to phenyl B; but after Doebner and amide, the phenyl B already has the unsaturated amide substituent; the sulfonyl chloride would be on the same phenyl B at para position relative to that substituent. So the sulfonyl chloride must be introduced before Doebner? Actually sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl B at the position where the sulfonamide attaches to p-tolyl. In target, phenyl B has sulfonamide at para to the unsaturated amide side chain. So we could start with phenyl B bearing sulfonyl chloride (para-chlorosulfonyl) and aldehyde (maybe ortho? but they are para to each other). So we need a starting material that has both aldehyde and sulfonyl chloride on same ring. That might be commercially available? Possibly 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride. That would have aldehyde and sulfonyl chloride para to each other. Then Doebner modification on aldehyde to give unsaturated acid (still attached to sulfonyl chloride). Then amide formation with aniline to give amide. Then sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine to give final product. That's 3 steps (Doebner, amide, sulfonamide). The order in forward: 1) Doebner (aldehyde + malonic acid) -> unsaturated acid. 2) Amide coupling (acid + aniline) -> amide. 3) Sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + p-toluidine) -> sulfonamide. That matches guidance (they gave order enumerated as they must be applied). So retrosynthesis order reversed: Step 3 (retro) break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl) and p-toluidine. Step 2 (retro) break amide to give unsaturated acid and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Step 1 (retro) break unsaturated acid to give aldehyde (4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride) and malonic acid.

Thus we need templates for each step. We need to find template IDs for sulfonamide formation, amide formation, Doebner modification. We have some template IDs from search results: For sulfonamide formation, we have template 1264686 (retro_smarts for sulfonamide formation). That template seems to go from sulfonamide to sulfonyl chloride + amine? Let's examine: retro_smarts_template: '[#7:3]-[S;H0;D4;+0:4](-[C;D1;H3:5])(=[O;H0;D1;+0:2])=[O;H0;D1;+0:1]>>C-C(-O)=[O;H0;D1;+0:1].O-[OH;D1;+0:2].[#7:3]-[S;H0;D2;+0:4]-[C;D1;H3:5]'

This seems to break sulfonamide into sulfonyl chloride? Actually product side is sulfonamide; reactant side includes sulfonyl chloride? The retro template shows product (left) is sulfonamide? The arrow direction: retro_smarts_template: product >> precursors. So left side is product (sulfonamide) and right side are precursors: C-C(-O)=O (maybe carbonyl?), O-[OH] (maybe HCl?), and amine + sulfonyl chloride? Actually the right side includes '[#7:3]-[S;H0;D2;+0:4]-[C;D1;H3:5]' which is sulfonyl chloride? Not sure. But we can use this template ID 1264686 for sulfonamide formation.

For amide formation, we need a template that breaks amide to acid + amine. Search didn't return but maybe there is a template. Could search for amide formation with functional groups broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, primary amines formed: amide. Let's try search with functional_groups_broken: ["aliphatic carboxylic acid","primary amines"], functional_groups_formed: ["amide"].
